executivePulse.interpretation: The situation for memory and AI infrastructure remains strained. Server DRAM / RDIMM, HBM and enterprise SSDs are currently among the most constrained segments. Calculation dated 2026-09-15; sources as of 2026-09-11. The evidence review is not yet complete (525 candidates open). The unchanged indicator therefore does not confirm an unchanged market environment. New capacity and improved yields can ease pressure but will reach the market only with a time lag. For buyers, securing supply, alternative BOMs and early procurement remain critical.

signals.title: OpenAI is working with Anthropic, Google on AI safety, Bloomberg News reports
signals.summary: Aktuelle Meldung von Reuters: OpenAI is working with Anthropic, Google on AI safety, Bloomberg News reports
signals.analysis: This report alters the build-out trajectory for AI and data centre infrastructure. Additional productive compute capacity will pull demand for server memory, enterprise storage, networking and power delivery, intensifying pressure on those supply chains.

signals.title: OpenAI, Google, Anthropic discussing collaboration on AI safety issues
signals.summary: Aktuelle Meldung von CNBC: OpenAI, Google, Anthropic discussing collaboration on AI safety issues
signals.analysis: The discussion implies coordinated scaling of safe AI deployments, which increases the need for reliable compute. That will raise demand for server memory, enterprise storage, networking and power provisioning across data centres.

signals.title: SK Hynix Is Shipping 16-Layer HBM4 for Nvidia Rubin: Where Do Micron And Samsung Stand?

outlooks.headline: Tight through 2027, transition from 2028
outlooks.view: Near-term procurement risk remains high. A linear price increase through 2029 is not a robust base case.

scenarios.label: Base case
scenarios.regime: Shortage in 2027, smaller gap in 2028, broad balance by 2029

scenarios.label: Structural shortage
scenarios.regime: Demand exceeds realisable output; high pricing and rationing persist

scenarios.label: Normalisation
scenarios.regime: Demand adjustment and new capacity drive materially lower pricing from 2028

timeline.label: Tight market regime
timeline.detail: High pricing, constrained qualified supply and active procurement adjustment.

timeline.label: Still tight
timeline.detail: Uncommitted or specially qualified server products remain particularly exposed.

timeline.label: Transition
timeline.detail: Larger supply contributions raise the probability of falling prices.

timeline.label: Balance becomes more plausible
timeline.detail: Broader normalisation becomes more likely; structural shortage remains a minority scenario.

changeRules.label: Contract pricing
changeRules.condition: Two consecutive quarters down by at least 10%

changeRules.label: Lead times
changeRules.condition: Confirmed lead times below eight weeks alongside rising qualified supply

changeRules.label: Capacity ramps
changeRules.condition: Two major DRAM ramps delay qualified supply by at least two quarters

changeRules.label: Host-bit demand
changeRules.condition: Comparable requested host bits grow by more than 25% YoY for two quarters without broad configuration cuts

outlooks.methodologyNote: Scenario weights are subjective, evidence-based assessments rather than statistically estimated event frequencies.

outlooks.headline: 2026 remains tight; normalisation risk rises from 2027
outlooks.view: Current market pressure remains high, but a permanently rising Enterprise SSD price path is not the base case. Qualified output, QLC scaling, buyer resistance and Chinese substitution can materially ease conditions from 2027/2028.
outlooks.researchReferenceNote: 83 is the market-pressure reference confirmed by the Astra audit, not a price target or a 2029 shortage probability. The operational live index continues to be calculated solely by the MT·AI index model.

scenarios.label: Base case
scenarios.regime: 2027 stabilisation; increasing easing pressure in 2028 and 2029. Price index Q3 2026=100: 85-115 / 65-95 / 55-85.

scenarios.label: Structural shortage
scenarios.regime: Qualified output trails real AI/data-centre deployment. Price index: 115-150 / 125-175 / 120-180.

scenarios.label: Normalisation / oversupply
scenarios.regime: QLC ramps, allocation shifts, the inventory cycle and Chinese substitution ease the market. Price index: 65-90 / 40-65 / 35-60.

timeline.label: High-priced and product-specific tightness
timeline.detail: Critical qualified volumes remain constrained; pricing and availability differ materially by TLC/QLC, capacity class and platform qualification.

timeline.label: Stabilisation in the base case
timeline.detail: Price band 85-115 relative to Q3 2026=100. At least one negative price quarter is plausible without implying broad availability of qualified high-capacity SKUs.

timeline.label: Easing risk rises
timeline.detail: Base-case price band 65-95. Technology, QLC and potential new wafer output matter only once they become genuinely qualified Enterprise SSD volumes.

timeline.label: Competition and supply discipline
timeline.detail: Base-case price band 55-85. Long-term uncertainty is high; structural shortage remains a separate stress case.

changeRules.label: Price + fulfilment + output
changeRules.condition: Two completed negative quarters for a comparable Enterprise SSD contract basket, plus better on-time fulfilment and rising qualified output

changeRules.label: Price + fill rate + deployment
changeRules.condition: Positive price quarters, weaker fill rates and stronger real deployment while qualified ramps miss plan

changeRules.label: Same-SKU channel
changeRules.condition: Repeated executable lower offers for the same SKU, volume and terms alongside improved availability

changeRules.label: Allocation cuts
changeRules.condition: Binding allocation cuts across multiple qualified Enterprise SSD product families

watchSignals: Customer inventory, cancellations and RFQ conversion

commercialDecision.buyer: For 2027, a heuristic starting point is to secure roughly 60% of conservatively confirmed demand by volume and keep 40% flexible; for 2028, secure about 30% of minimum demand and keep 70% flexible. Secure supply while resetting pricing periodically where possible.
commercialDecision.seller: Avoid uncommitted speculative inventory in high-priced Enterprise SSDs. Hold 30.72/61.44 TB only against dated recurring call-offs or matched orders; source 122.88/245 TB against named customer demand. Offer long fixed prices only with matched supplier protection.

outlooks.methodologyNote: Market-pressure index and price forecast remain separate. Scenario weights of 50/20/30 are HEURISTIC rather than statistically calibrated event frequencies. Missing data is not a relief signal; correlated evidence is not double-counted.
